more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Alginic acid is a polysaccharide from brown seaweeds, consisting mainly of linked mannuronic and guluronic acid units. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. Extracted from brown seaweeds with dilute alkali. The recovered material is a polysaccharide made mainly of mannuronic and guluronic acid units. The specified material is supplied as white powder or granules. The specification describes it as effectively insoluble in water.
more_info.origin: Extracted from brown seaweeds with dilute alkali. The recovered material is a polysaccharide made mainly of mannuronic and guluronic acid units.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
The 2017 assessment identified uncertainty for medically vulnerable infants.
Therapeutic doses can cause side effects; those conclusions require population-specific interpretation.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
